title: The Little Dinosaur's Way Home
opening: Milo and the camp guide have lost their paper route. Nobody is in danger. Your explorer team must compare footprints, repair a map, choose a paper supply pack and find the welcoming camp. Every piece you need is printed in this pack.
ending: Milo waves from Camp A. Your SUN trail reached PINE SIGN; the supply pack gave code 4; the signpost led EAST to a ROUND gate. You checked the clues together and helped Milo find the right camp. Welcome home, explorers!

stages.title: Find Milo's footprint
stages.story: Milo has THREE toes, a ROUND heel and ONE notch on the RIGHT edge. Match all three features. The route start belongs to the matching footprint.
hints: Count the toes first.
Check heel and right notch as well.
Print A matches all three; take SUN.
stages.next: Use the recorded discovery on the next mission.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Print A; SUN. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

stages.title: Repair the trail map
stages.story: Begin at your previous route start. Join each strip's TO place to the next strip's FROM place. The correct trail must end at a SIGN. Lay the route on the table; keep rejected strips beside it.
hints: Find both strips starting at SUN.
Only one branch can end at a sign; CAVE ends at ROCK.
A-B-C leads to PINE SIGN.
stages.next: Use the recorded discovery on the next mission.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with A-B-C: SUN-FERN-RIVER-PINE SIGN. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

stages.title: Choose the paper supplies
stages.story: Combine THREE explorer notes: use the sign from your route, exactly TWO straps, and a TRIANGLE tag. PINE SIGN is shortened to PINE on the pack cards. Choose the same card satisfying every clue. These are paper records, not real bags.
hints: Share all three notes.
Reject one wrong feature at a time.
Pack B matches PINE, two straps and triangle; code 4.
role_cards: Use the sign from the repaired trail. PINE SIGN means PINE.
The pack must have exactly TWO straps.
The pack must have a TRIANGLE tag.
stages.next: Use the recorded discovery on the next mission.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Pack B; code 4. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

stages.title: Build the signpost
stages.story: Take BOTH inputs from your record: the sign and the pack code. Only one row matches both. Reader checks the sign, Investigator checks the code, Recorder writes the turn and gate, Checker rejects another row. Say the turn and draw the gate shape on your record. No one leaves the table.
hints: You need two inputs.
PINE alone leaves three rows; also match 4.
PINE + 4 gives EAST / ROUND.
stages.next: Use the recorded discovery on the next mission.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Row B; EAST / ROUND. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

stages.title: Find the welcoming camp
stages.story: Compare ALL FOUR discoveries: start, sign, turn and gate. Choose the camp matching every field. Each player checks a field; explain TWO earlier clues to your host. PINE SIGN means PINE.
hints: Read the four discoveries aloud.
One wrong field rules out a camp.
Camp A matches SUN, PINE, EAST and ROUND.
stages.next: Use the recorded discovery on the next mission.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Camp A. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

title: The Lost Space Signal
opening: Pip the little robot probe has sent a paper signal from somewhere in the story sky. Find the true message, follow the star map and send a pretend reply. All equipment is made of paper.
ending: After the team identifies Probe A using at least two different clues, read: 'Pip received your message. Your team found the true signal by sharing every clue.' Do not require a real transmitter, app, electrical device or online account.

stages.title: Find the real signal
stages.story: The real signal has a ROUND border, THREE waves and ONE square gap at the lower right. Compare all three printed attributes.
stages.next: Only the star-map route beginning at your sector can lead to a numbered station.
hints: Check border, waves and gap separately.
All three properties must match at once.
Card C; give ORION.
stages.card_note: Compare all four pictured signals. Each border, wave count and gap has a matching text label; no colour clue is needed. Keep cards on this page or let an adult cut them.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Card C; ORION. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

stages.title: Repair the star map
stages.story: Start from the sector in your record. Join strips where the end of one matches the start of another. The useful path ends at a NUMBERED STATION.
stages.next: The station number is one of three facts needed to select a paper device.
hints: Match printed end and start names.
One ORION path ends in EMPTY FIELD; find the numbered station.
A-B-C; give STATION 7.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with A-B-C; STATION 7. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

stages.title: Share calibration clues
stages.story: Give Guide, Robot and Scout one clue line each. Read every clue aloud and choose one paper device. Guide: use your numbered station. Robot: TWO rings. Scout: TRIANGLE badge.
stages.next: Only the dictionary labelled with your device code is used in the paper message.
hints: Let each role read one fact.
Intersect Station 7, two rings and triangle.
Device B; give Code 6.
role_cards: Use the numbered station from your map.
The paper device has TWO rings.
The paper device has a TRIANGLE badge.
stages.card_note: These are paper props. Count rings and compare badge outlines with the three role clues; the printed labels give the same facts.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Device B; Code 6. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

stages.title: Decode Pip's message
stages.story: Use the code on your chosen paper device. Replace each printed symbol in order using that code's dictionary row. No outside space knowledge is needed.
stages.extra: Use only your selected device code. Paper message: SUN / MOON / STAR / PATH / RING
stages.next: The decoded word is a label on exactly one fully matching probe record.
hints: Start with the first symbol.
Keep the printed order when replacing symbols.
COMET; give the word to players.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with COMET. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.
actions: Read the device code on your checkpoint 3 record. Find the dictionary card with that SAME code.
Reader calls the printed message symbols one at a time: SUN, MOON, STAR, PATH, RING.
Investigator points to each symbol's letter on that single dictionary card. Recorder writes five letters left to right.
Checker rechecks the code and each lookup. Join the letters into a word and record it; do not take a letter from another code row.

stages.title: Send the pretend reply
stages.story: Compare your sector, station, code and decoded word with every probe record. Circle the only record matching all four. Tell your grown-up two facts that prove it.
stages.next: Your adult can read Pip's paper reply card.
hints: Use the record sheet, not the illustration.
Each wrong probe differs in at least one field.
Probe A; read Pip's reply.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Probe A. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

title: The Forest Post Office Mystery
opening: A rain shower has blurred one paper parcel label. Help Nori the forest post carrier use postmark and route records to deliver it to the right story character. Every address is fictional.
ending: After players identify Delivery Card A with at least two reasons, read Nori's note: 'The label is clear again. Your careful record helped this parcel reach the right story home.' No real address, mailbox or outdoor walk is required.

stages.title: Find the matching postmark
stages.story: The task postmark has a LEAF border, TWO stars and the weekday TUE. Match all three printed parts.
stages.next: Only route strips for your batch belong to the blurred parcel.
hints: Inspect all three postmark properties.
Border, star count and day must all match.
Card B; give M2.
stages.card_note: Compare the leaf or moon outline, star count and day together. Each printed label repeats the pictured clue; no colour clue is needed.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Card B; M2. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

stages.title: Follow the paper route
stages.story: Use ONLY strips carrying your batch mark. Start at POST OFFICE and join matching place names. The useful path ends at a named tree with both colour and words.
stages.next: Take the district name to the parcel-sorting cards.
hints: Keep only the correct batch's strips.
Join the M2 place names from POST OFFICE to the named tree.
A-B-C; give BLUE TREE.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with A-B-C; BLUE TREE. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.
actions: Read your batch mark from checkpoint 1. Investigator separates strips with that SAME batch; park every other batch.
Start at POST OFFICE. Join FROM/TO names on the remaining strips; lay the chain left to right.
Checker verifies each join and that the chain ends at a named tree. Do not use an excluded batch to extend the trail.
Recorder writes the strip letters and the complete district name, including colour; everyone traces the route.

stages.title: Share the parcel clues
stages.story: Carrier: use your route district. Sorter: the parcel has TWO leaf marks. Keeper: its paper outline is ROUND. Share all three facts before circling a card.
stages.next: Your parcel's address fragment and district together identify the recipient marker.
hints: Let each role say a different clue.
Intersect district, two leaves and round outline.
Parcel C; give W4.
role_cards: Use the district from your paper route.
The parcel has TWO leaf marks.
The parcel has a ROUND paper outline.
stages.card_note: The picture and printed labels show the same clues. A grown-up may cut each parcel card, or the group can compare them here.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Parcel C; W4. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

stages.title: Repair the story address
stages.story: On the fictional forest map, find the block matching BOTH your district and your parcel's fragment.
stages.next: The recipient marker is the last field in Nori's delivery record.
hints: Look up district and fragment together.
BLUE TREE has more than one row; inspect the fragment.
OWL HOUSE; give this marker.
stages.card_note: Keep the four-block map intact. Match the place and printed fragment together before recording a recipient.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with OWL HOUSE. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

stages.title: Deliver the story parcel
stages.story: Compare batch, district, fragment and recipient marker. Circle the only card matching every discovery. Give your grown-up two reasons.
stages.next: The grown-up can read Nori's paper thank-you note.
hints: Use the record sheet, not the art.
Every wrong card differs in one field.
Card A; read Nori's note.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Delivery Card A. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

title: The Missing Pumpkin Light
opening: Pip's pretend paper pumpkin lantern has gone dim. Four paper seals can make the festival picture bright again. Find the seals and put them in the order written in the final note. There is no real light or flame.
ending: Once the children assemble 5-7-2-3 in the decoded SUN-MOON-HAT-STAR order, unfold a paper picture or read: 'Everyone's clue helped the festival picture shine.' This is a pretend paper-lit ending, never a request to light anything.

stages.title: Find Pip's letter
stages.story: Pip's letter has a FOX-shaped seal, TWO stars and a MOON postmark. Find the card matching all three parts.
stages.next: Use the start word on Pip's letter to follow the paper festival map.
hints: Check seal, stars and postmark.
All three printed properties must match.
Letter C; give SUN=5 and GATE.
stages.card_note: Compare seal picture, star count and postmark together. The printed labels repeat each visual clue; no colour is needed.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Letter C; SUN=5 and GATE. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

stages.title: Repair the festival map
stages.story: Use ONLY strips with Pip's GATE start and join matching place names. The useful route reaches PARCEL TABLE, not END.
stages.next: The parcel batch helps the crew find Pip's decorated paper parcel.
hints: Join names from GATE.
The SHED path stops; continue to PARCEL TABLE.
A-B-C; give MOON=7 and P3.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with A-B-C; MOON=7 and P3. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

stages.title: Share the parcel clues
stages.story: Courier: use the batch from the map. Decorator: look for TWO stripes. Keeper: choose a ROUNDED paper outline. Compare every card.
stages.next: The parcel letter chooses which dictionary row to use on the reply card.
hints: Each role reads a different condition.
Intersect P3, two stripes and round outline.
Parcel B; give HAT=2 and row B.
role_cards: Use the parcel batch from your paper map.
The parcel has a ROUNDED paper outline.
stages.card_note: The picture and printed labels show the same clues. An adult may cut the four choice cards, or players can compare them on this page.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Parcel B; HAT=2. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

stages.title: Decode the paper reply
stages.story: Use the dictionary ROW labelled with your chosen parcel. Replace the four code words in the printed order. Read the STAR seal value from the same row.
stages.next: Write each seal's number in the decoded order on the final paper lantern card.
hints: Use the parcel letter, not the first row.
Replace KITE-TREE-ACORN-FLAG in that order.
Row B; STAR=3, order SUN-MOON-HAT-STAR.
stages.extra: Encoded reply: KITE / TREE / ACORN / FLAG
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Parcel B row; SUN-MOON-HAT-STAR; STAR=3. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.
actions: Read the chosen parcel LETTER from checkpoint 3. Select the dictionary card with the SAME row letter.
Reader reads KITE, TREE, ACORN, FLAG in that order. Investigator points to each corresponding seal name on the selected row.
Recorder writes those four seal names in order. Checker repeats the lookups on the same row.
Read the STAR value from that row and add it to your record. Keep the ordered seal names for checkpoint 5.

stages.title: Complete the paper lantern
stages.story: Write each discovered number on its named paper seal. Put the four seals in the order from the reply, then circle the matching four-digit card. No real light is needed.
stages.next: The grown-up can show the safe paper festival picture.
hints: Write seal names before numbers.
Use SUN=5, MOON=7, HAT=2 and STAR=3 in the decoded order.
5723; read the paper ending.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Card A; 5723. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.
actions: Retrieve your record: copy the SUN value from checkpoint 1, MOON from 2, HAT from 3 and STAR from 4 onto the FOUR named blank seal cards.
Investigator arranges the seals in the exact seal-name order decoded at checkpoint 4. All four names must be used once.
Reader reads the four numbers left to right; Recorder joins them into one four-digit code without rearranging them.
Checker finds that code among the final candidates and asks each player to trace one number to its original clue. Show the code and evidence to your adult.

title: The Christmas Delivery Office
opening: The story delivery office has mixed up its last paper list. Match pretend gift cards with story destinations and find the final thank-you note. No one needs to buy, exchange or wrap a real gift.
ending: After players select Delivery Card A and explain two clues, read: 'The messenger finished the paper route. Every story friend has a matching picture card. Thank you for checking the list together.' Any family reward is an adult's optional separate choice.

stages.title: Choose the right list
stages.story: The task label has a SNOWFLAKE frame, TWO round dots and a STAR print. Match every property.
stages.next: Use only gift cards from the chosen batch.
hints: Check frame, dots and print.
All three details must match together.
Card A; give B3.
stages.card_note: Compare frame picture, dot count and print picture together. Every visual clue is repeated in the label; no colour is needed.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Card A; B3. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

stages.title: Match the picture gifts
stages.story: Use only your batch. Owl wants the ROUND picture at OWL WINDOW; Fox wants the SQUARE picture at FOX DEN; Rabbit wants the TRIANGLE picture at RABBIT GATE. These are imaginary characters.
stages.next: All three places must appear exactly once in the paper route.
hints: First remove the wrong batch.
Match each shape to the stated character and place.
A-Owl, B-Fox, C-Rabbit; keep their places.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with A-Owl, B-Fox, C-Rabbit. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.
actions: Read the batch from checkpoint 1. Remove gift cards belonging to a different batch.
Put the three destination cards across the table. Read each character's requested picture shape aloud.
Investigator places each remaining gift under the destination with its matching shape. Checker makes sure each gift and destination are used once.
Recorder writes all THREE gift-letter/character/place pairs. Keep the matched gifts accessible for the next route task.

stages.title: Share the route conditions
stages.story: Use your gift-to-place pairs from Checkpoint 2. Guide: FOX DEN comes BEFORE OWL WINDOW. Clock: RABBIT GATE is LAST. Map: visit the three places once. Put the gift LETTERS in route order.
stages.next: Only the last place has the coded paper thank-you note.
hints: Use the three gift-to-place pairs first.
Rabbit's gift is last and Fox's gift comes before Owl's.
Route B: gifts B-A-C; give FOX-OWL-RABBIT.
role_cards: FOX DEN comes BEFORE OWL WINDOW.
Visit all three paper places exactly once.
stages.card_note: The picture and printed labels show the same order. An adult may cut the four cards, or players can compare them on this page; read all role clues before choosing.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Route B; FOX-OWL-RABBIT. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.
actions: Retrieve the three matched gift cards from your checkpoint 2 evidence pile. Read the three route clue cards aloud.
Investigator lays the gifts in a route satisfying BEFORE and LAST. Use each destination exactly once.
Checker compares that order with the printed route candidates and explains why another route fails.
Recorder writes gift LETTERS in route order and the last destination. Leave the matching pairs in the evidence area.

stages.title: Read the final paper note
stages.story: Find the envelope for the LAST place on your route. Use the printed dictionary in order; the note is pretend and no one needs to go anywhere.
stages.next: Use both last place and note on the final delivery card.
hints: Choose the route's final place.
Replace TREE, STAR, MOON without sorting them.
RABBIT GATE; give GO!.
stages.extra: Dictionary: TREE = G / STAR = O / MOON = !
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with RABBIT GATE; GO!. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.
actions: Read the LAST destination from the route you solved at checkpoint 3. Find the envelope addressed to that place.
Reader reads its code symbols from left to right. Investigator points to each symbol in the printed TREE/STAR/MOON dictionary.
Recorder writes one character for each symbol, keeping punctuation. Join the characters into the pretend message.
Checker verifies both the envelope destination and every dictionary lookup. Record the last place and the whole message.

stages.title: Check the final delivery
stages.story: Compare batch, route order, last place and note. Circle the only card matching all four and tell your grown-up two reasons.
stages.next: The grown-up can read the paper thank-you note.
hints: Use the full record sheet.
Each other card changes one field.
Card A; read the thank-you note.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Delivery Card A. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

title: The Coral Chart Expedition
opening: The research ship has five loose pages from a fictional survey. Work as a crew to rebuild the route and send the captain one checked report.
ending: The captain thanks your crew. The repaired chart can guide the next pretend paper expedition.

stages.title: Find the survey station
stages.story: The log says: choose the station with a BLUE flag and exactly THREE wave marks. Colour words and counts are both printed; do not rely on colour alone.
rows: Reef A | blue flag | two waves
Reef B | blue flag | three waves
Reef C | red flag | three waves
prompts: Which station should the crew inspect?
stages.next: Give the crew BLUE-3 and move to the chart.
hints: Read both conditions in the log.
A station with only one matching condition is not enough.
Reef B has blue and three waves.
stages.why: Only Reef B has both the blue flag and three waves.

stages.title: Locate the chart square
stages.story: Find your station code in this chart key: BLUE-2 = A1; BLUE-3 = C2; RED-3 = D4. Use the code from the log, not a guess from the drawing.
prompts: Which square matches the log code?
stages.next: Give the crew C2 and continue with the observation cards.
hints: Keep the complete code from checkpoint 1.
Read the middle row of the key.
BLUE-3 points to C2.
stages.why: The key maps BLUE-3 to C2.

stages.title: Compare the three observations
stages.story: At C2, the Navigator says the route must touch a buoy. The Observer says it must avoid the red marker. The Recorder says it must pass east of the square.
rows: North Passage | buoy | red marker | west
East Passage | buoy | no red marker | east
South Passage | no buoy | no red marker | east
prompts: Which passage satisfies all three crew notes?
stages.next: Give the crew EAST; keep the role evidence for the final report.
hints: Share all three role notes.
Cross out any passage with a red marker or no buoy.
East Passage satisfies all conditions.
stages.why: Only East Passage has a buoy, no red marker and an eastward position.
role_cards: At C2, the route must touch a buoy.
At C2, the route must avoid the red marker.
At C2, the route must pass EAST of the square.

stages.title: Order the record strips
stages.story: The EAST passage record says the Kelp note came first, the Reef note came after Kelp, and the Channel note came last.
prompts: What is the correct record order?
stages.next: Give the crew K-R-C for the report.
hints: Place the first and last strips before the middle.
K is first and C is last.
The remaining R sits between them.
stages.why: Kelp first, Reef next and Channel last makes K-R-C.

stages.title: Send the captain's report
stages.story: A valid report must include the station code, chart square, passage and record order that your crew earned. Compare your written results with the three candidate reports.
prompts: Which report is fully supported by your paper evidence?
stages.next: Use Report 1 and read the ending.
hints: Read the results in checkpoint order.
Check the square and passage before the final order.
All four results match Report 1.
stages.why: Report 1 is the only report consistent with all four earlier results.

title: The Mixed-Up Exhibition
opening: A fictional museum opens tomorrow, but one exhibit label has wandered away. Your curators must compare marks, case notes and a floor plan to put it back.
ending: The exhibit is ready. Visitors can read its correct fictional story because your curators checked every clue.

stages.title: Read the lost ticket
stages.story: The ticket shows TWO crescent marks and ONE star. The gallery ledger says: Amber has two crescents and one star; Blue has one crescent and two stars; Green has two crescents and no star.
stages.next: Give the curators AMBER.
hints: Count both kinds of mark.
Two crescents are not enough without the star.
Amber matches all three marks.
stages.why: Amber alone matches both crescent count and star count.

stages.title: Walk the gallery route
stages.story: The Amber floor plan says: start at the door, go past Case 2, then turn right to the case beside the window. The window-side cases are Case 4 and Case 7; only Case 4 is to the right of Case 2.
rows: Case 4 | right of Case 2, by window
prompts: Which case is on the ticket route?
stages.next: Give the curators CASE-4.
hints: The destination is not the case you pass.
Use right and window together.
Choose Case 4.
stages.why: Case 4 is both right of Case 2 and beside the window.

stages.title: Identify the curious object
stages.story: In Case 4, the Object keeper sees a folded wing. The Map keeper's inventory says the object has a round dial. The Label keeper's note says it is made of paper.
rows: Clockwork Kite | folded wing, round dial, paper
Sun Compass | no wing, round dial, paper
Silver Moth | folded wing, no dial, metal
prompts: Which invented object fits all three records?
stages.next: Give the curators KITE.
hints: Each role has one necessary fact.
Reject objects that fail even one fact.
Clockwork Kite is the only full match.
stages.why: Only Clockwork Kite has a wing, dial and paper material.
role_cards: In Case 4, the object has a folded wing.
In Case 4, the object has a ROUND dial.
In Case 4, the object is made of PAPER.

stages.title: Restore the object label
stages.story: The Clockwork Kite record says it is a pretend paper instrument for tracing an imaginary breeze. Do not choose a label about real history or a powered machine.
rows: Label A | A royal metal clock from 1800
Label B | A pretend paper breeze-tracing kite
Label C | A motorised weather balloon
prompts: Which label tells the object's true fictional story?
stages.next: Give the curators LABEL-B.
hints: Keep the object fictional.
Look for paper and breeze.
Label B says both.
stages.why: Label B matches the invented paper object's stated purpose.

stages.title: Complete the exhibition sheet
stages.story: The opening sheet needs the gallery, case, object and label already found. A wrong field means visitors would see the wrong exhibit.
rows: Sheet A | Amber / Case 4 / Clockwork Kite / Label B
Sheet B | Blue / Case 4 / Clockwork Kite / Label B
Sheet C | Amber / Case 7 / Silver Moth / Label A
prompts: Which opening sheet uses the complete evidence trail?
stages.next: Use Sheet A and read the ending.
hints: Read your four earlier results in order.
Check gallery and case first.
All fields on Sheet A match.
stages.why: Sheet A agrees with each prior result.

title: The Missing Final Chapter
opening: A fictional storybook has lost its final page. Each reading group holds a different clue. Put the pages back in order before choosing the ending that fits.
ending: The librarian places the recovered page into the book. The story can now be read from beginning to end.

stages.title: Follow the index symbol
stages.story: The missing book's index slip has a BLUE moon above a small key. Shelf M has blue moon and key; Shelf P has blue star and key; Shelf T has red moon and key.
stages.next: Give the group SHELF-M.
hints: Match both symbol and colour word.
A star is not a moon.
Shelf M has the exact pair.
stages.why: Shelf M matches both the blue moon and key.

stages.title: Find the page bundle
stages.story: The Shelf M ledger says the book has SEVEN paper leaves and a violet ribbon. Bundle M7 has seven leaves and violet ribbon; M4 has four leaves; P7 has seven leaves but is on another shelf.
prompts: Which bundle should the group open?
stages.next: Give the group M7.
hints: Keep the shelf letter from the index.
Count leaves and check ribbon.
M7 matches every detail.
stages.why: M7 matches shelf, leaf count and ribbon.

stages.title: Put the middle events in order
stages.story: The M7 pages say the Lantern is lit before anyone crosses the Bridge. The Garden gate opens only after the crossing. The three role readers each hold one of those facts.
prompts: What is the only possible story order?
stages.next: Give the group L-B-G.
hints: Find the event that must happen first.
The Garden cannot precede the Bridge.
The order is L-B-G.
stages.why: Lantern must precede Bridge, and Garden follows Bridge.
role_cards: The Lantern is lit BEFORE anyone crosses the Bridge.
The Bridge crossing happens AFTER the Lantern is lit.
The Garden gate opens only AFTER the crossing.

stages.title: Read the final-page index
stages.story: The librarian's index maps story orders to page pockets: L-G-B goes to Pocket 2; L-B-G goes to Pocket 9; B-L-G goes to Pocket 5.
stages.next: Give the group PAGE-9.
hints: Use your sequence exactly.
Do not swap Bridge and Garden.
Look in Pocket 9.
stages.why: The correct earlier order L-B-G maps to Pocket 9.

stages.title: Choose a fitting ending
stages.story: The recovered Page 9 says the group used the lantern to guide friends safely across, then shared a map of the garden. The ending must follow that action without adding a new unexplained quest.
rows: Ending A | They hid the lantern and forgot the garden.
Ending B | They shared the garden map and went home together.
Ending C | A rocket appeared and took everyone to the Moon.
stages.next: Use Ending B and read the librarian's reply.
hints: The ending should grow from Page 9.
Avoid new events without clues.
Ending B continues the shared map story.
stages.why: Ending B follows the recovered page's sharing and group journey.

title: The Lost Forecast Bulletin
opening: The paper observatory lost its fictional bulletin. Three teams each hold one type of symbol card. Compare the printed rules and rebuild the notice.
ending: The station posts its pretend bulletin. Every symbol can be checked against the paper key your team used.

stages.title: Choose the observation day
stages.story: The station mark is a BLUE triangle above TWO short lines. Day 3 has blue triangle + two lines; Day 1 has blue triangle + one line; Day 5 has red triangle + two lines.
prompts: Which day belongs to this station mark?
stages.next: Give the class DAY-3.
hints: Check the triangle and line count.
Two lines alone do not decide the day.
Day 3 has both marks.
stages.why: Day 3 matches both the colour word and two lines.

stages.title: Find the map grid
stages.story: The date chart gives Day 1 -> A1, Day 3 -> B2, Day 5 -> C3. The answer is a map grid, not a weather prediction.
prompts: Which grid should the teams inspect?
stages.next: Give the class B2.
hints: Bring the exact day from checkpoint 1.
Read the middle date-chart row.
Inspect B2.
stages.why: Day 3 maps to B2.

stages.title: Combine the symbol teams
stages.story: At B2, Cloud readers report TWO cloud circles. Wind readers report an arrow pointing RIGHT. Rain readers report ONE drop. All three printed facts are needed.
rows: Set A | 2 clouds, right arrow, 1 drop
Set B | 2 clouds, left arrow, 1 drop
Set C | 1 cloud, right arrow, 2 drops
stages.next: Give the class SET-A.
hints: Ask all three teams to speak.
Check arrow direction after counting symbols.
Set A is the full match.
stages.why: Set A alone has two clouds, right arrow and one drop.
role_cards: At B2, there are TWO cloud circles.
At B2, the wind arrow points RIGHT.
At B2, there is ONE drop.

stages.title: Put the bulletin strips in order
stages.story: For Set A, the station rule says wind is announced first, cloud second and rain last. These are pretend symbol categories, not a real forecast.
prompts: What is the correct bulletin order?
stages.next: Give the class W-C-R.
hints: Find the first and last categories.
W comes first, R last.
C belongs between W and R.
stages.why: The printed Set A rule places W before C before R.

stages.title: Post the checked bulletin
stages.story: The station posts only a sheet with the day, map grid, complete symbol set and strip order your teams verified.
rows: Sheet A | Day 3 / B2 / Set A / W-C-R
Sheet B | Day 3 / C3 / Set A / W-C-R
Sheet C | Day 5 / B2 / Set B / C-W-R
prompts: Which sheet is supported by the paper observations?
stages.next: Use Sheet A and read the station ending.
hints: Check the day before the symbols.
One wrong field invalidates a bulletin.
All four fields match Sheet A.
stages.why: Sheet A is the only sheet matching all previous outputs.

title: The Great Blueprint Relay
opening: The workshop's paper-only pretend machine has lost its display blueprint. Teams need to choose the correct sheet, combine three safety notes and explain the order on paper. Nothing is built or powered.
ending: The inventor pins up the checked paper blueprint. Visitors can follow the pretend idea without handling a real tool.

stages.title: Find the design code
stages.story: The inventory slip calls for a TRIANGLE gear mark and TWO square tabs. P7 has triangle gear + two tabs; P4 has triangle gear + one tab; Q7 has circle gear + two tabs.
stages.next: Give the team P7.
hints: Use both the gear shape and tab count.
Two tabs without the right gear are not enough.
P7 matches everything.
stages.why: P7 matches both printed marks.

stages.title: Pick the blueprint sheet
stages.story: The P7 register calls for a long base with two round windows. Frame B has both; Frame A has one window; Frame C has two windows but a short base.
rows: Frame A | long base, one window
Frame B | long base, two windows
Frame C | short base, two windows
stages.next: Give the team FRAME-B.
hints: Keep the P7 register in view.
Check both base length and window count.
Choose Frame B.
stages.why: Frame B alone matches the long base and two windows.

stages.title: Share the three constraint cards
stages.story: For Frame B, the Designer wants a BLUE paper gear. The Checker needs a SHORT paper belt. The Explainer needs a RED display flag. Compare all three role cards aloud.
rows: Kit 1 | blue gear, long belt, red flag
Kit 2 | blue gear, short belt, red flag
Kit 3 | yellow gear, short belt, red flag
prompts: Which paper kit fits every role?
stages.next: Give the team KIT-2.
hints: Each role contributes one condition.
A single wrong part rejects the kit.
Kit 2 satisfies all three.
stages.why: Kit 2 has the blue gear, short belt and red flag.
role_cards: For Frame B, use a BLUE paper gear.
For Frame B, use a SHORT paper belt.
For Frame B, use a RED display flag.

stages.title: Order the display cards
stages.story: The Kit 2 display rule says: FOLD the paper base first, ALIGN the printed gear symbol next, and TURN the paper instruction card last. These are story cards, not steps for a real mechanism.
prompts: Which written order belongs on the blueprint?
stages.next: Give the team F-A-T.
hints: Start with the base.
Turn the instruction card last.
Align belongs in the middle.
stages.why: The printed order is fold, align, turn.

stages.title: Complete the display blueprint
stages.story: The final sheet must list the correct design code, frame, kit and written card order. Keep this a paper display; no child has to make or operate a device.
rows: Board A | P7 / Frame B / Kit 2 / F-A-T
Board B | P7 / Frame C / Kit 2 / F-A-T
Board C | Q7 / Frame B / Kit 1 / A-F-T
prompts: Which board can the group explain with its evidence?
stages.next: Use Board A and read the workshop ending.
hints: Read the earlier results aloud.
Check every field, not only the title.
Board A agrees with all four checkpoints.
stages.why: Board A carries all four earned results in order.

title: The Adventure Club's First Badge
opening: The Adventure Club has left five paper clues. Find the invitation, repair a route, combine equipment clues and build a four-symbol badge. Every group has its own full clue set.
ending: Welcome to the Adventure Club! Your invitation led from GATE to WORKSHOP, equipment A gave 2-4-1-3, and your badge reads COMPASS, BOOK, STAR, HANDS clockwise. Draw those four symbols on your keepsake, starting at the top.

stages.title: Find the invitation
stages.story: Choose the invitation with a COMPASS seal and exactly TWO stars. Take its route start.
hints: Check the seal.
Also count both stars.
Card B gives GATE.
stages.next: Use the recorded discovery on the next mission.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Card B; GATE. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

stages.title: Repair the club route
stages.story: Start at your discovered place. Join FROM and TO place names. The useful route ends at WORKSHOP.
hints: Try the two GATE strips.
The garden route stops at SHED.
A-B-C reaches WORKSHOP.
stages.next: Use the recorded discovery on the next mission.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with A-B-C; WORKSHOP. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

stages.title: Choose the equipment
stages.story: Combine all three clues: BLUE, exactly TWO dots and TRIANGLE. Copy the code from the same matching card.
hints: Share each clue.
Every condition must fit the same card.
A gives 2-4-1-3.
stages.next: Use the recorded discovery on the next mission.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Equipment A; 2-4-1-3. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

stages.title: Build the badge pattern
stages.story: Use the code you earned. Each number names one symbol. Read your code in order; positions are TOP, RIGHT, BOTTOM, LEFT clockwise. Draw or write each symbol.
hints: Copy the equipment code first.
Replace each number with its symbol.
2-4-1-3 means COMPASS, BOOK, STAR, HANDS.
stages.next: Use the recorded discovery on the next mission.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with COMPASS / BOOK / STAR / HANDS. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.

stages.title: Check your badge plan
stages.story: Your plan must match the destination, equipment card and all four positions TOP-RIGHT-BOTTOM-LEFT. Check every field and explain two facts.
hints: Read all earlier results.
Check both place and symbol order.
Plan A matches every field.
stages.next: Use the recorded discovery on the next mission.
stages.why: Compare the stated conditions with Plan A. Each required field must match; a candidate with one wrong field is rejected.
